what_its_for: Sarecycline is an antibiotic used to treat moderate to severe acne (pimples and skin breakouts) in patients 9 years of age and older. It works by killing the bacteria on your skin that cause acne.
how_to_take: Take sarecycline by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you feel stomach upset, taking it with a small snack or meal may help.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the right dose based on your body weight. Common doses are 60 mg, 100 mg, or 150 mg taken once daily. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed — do not take more or less than directed. Do not stop taking it early, even if your skin starts looking better.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store sarecycline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking sarecycline within 2 hours of antacids (like Tums or Maalox), dairy products (milk, yogurt, cheese), iron supplements, calcium supplements, or vitamins that contain minerals — these can prevent the medication from working properly. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds while taking this medication, as it can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Always use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, diarrhea, or bloody stools; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe headache or blurred vision (which could be signs of increased pressure in the brain); vaginal yeast infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if your acne is getting significantly worse. Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant while taking this medication.
when_it_works: Sarecycline does not work overnight. Most patients begin to see improvement in their acne after about 3 months (12 weeks) of treatment. It is very important to keep taking the medication as directed even if you do not see results right away. Talk to your doctor at your follow-up visit if you have concerns about your progress.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Do not use sarecycline if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It can harm the unborn baby and may pass into breast milk. Children: Sarecycline is approved for children 9 years and older. It should NOT be used in children under 9 years of age because it can permanently stain developing teeth and affect bone growth. Kidney or Liver Problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, tell your doctor before starting this medication, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Elderly Patients: No specific dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but always inform your doctor of all your other medications.
